deck: This week sees increased consolidation and funding in space.

stories.head: Astrobotic sells to Voyager for lunar ambitions
stories.body: Astrobotic has been acquired by Voyager Technologies, allowing the former to scale operations for NASA's lunar initiatives. The terms of the deal were not disclosed, but it highlights the trend of companies seeking partnerships to navigate the complex lunar landscape. This acquisition might just be the lifeline Astrobotic needed to avoid becoming another footnote in lunar history.
stories.soWhat: Sometimes, the only way to make it to the moon is to hitch a ride with a better-funded partner.

stories.head: MDA Space spends $620 million on Blue Canyon
stories.body: MDA Space is acquiring Blue Canyon Technologies for $620 million, aiming to strengthen its foothold in the U.S. market. This move underscores the ongoing consolidation as companies look to bolster capabilities and market access. Blue Canyon's satellite technology will likely serve as a strategic asset for MDA's ambitions in the increasingly competitive U.S. sector.
stories.soWhat: In aerospace, buying your way in is often cheaper than building from scratch.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190 million amid co-orbital security demand
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190 million in Series C funding, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. This influx of capital reflects the growing interest in co-orbital security solutions as defense demands rise. The funding round suggests investors are banking on True Anomaly's potential to fill gaps in the military's space capabilities.
stories.soWhat: In a world where space is the new frontier for defense, cash is king, and True Anomaly is sitting on a throne.

watchlist.title: Jio's LEO constellation IPO plans
watchlist.body: India's Jio is gearing up for an IPO tied to its sovereign LEO constellation, which could reshape connectivity in the region.

watchlist.title: ElevationSpace's Series B implications
watchlist.body: With $40 million raised, ElevationSpace's focus on space transportation could signal a new wave of investment in launch capabilities.

watchlist.title: Northrop Grumman's solid rocket production
watchlist.body: As Northrop Grumman claims readiness to scale production, the industry will be watching for actual demand to materialize.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN contract extension
watchlist.body: Palantir's $480 million extension on the TITAN program could indicate a longer-term commitment to military space operations.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
